html:
The Kingdom of Kapisa was a state in what is now eastern Afghanistan in the late first millennium, named after its capital, Kapisa, near modern Bagram north of Kabul. It reached from the Hindu Kush to Bamiyan and east toward Jalalabad. The map shows it around 700.

The pilgrim Xuanzang passed through around 630 and found a rich, mainly Buddhist land with many monasteries. The great Buddhas of Bamiyan stood at its western edge. From the mid 600s it was ruled by the Turk Shahis, kings of Turkic origin who later moved their capital to Kabul.

For two centuries these kings fought off the armies of the Arab conquests, like their southern neighbours the Zunbils. In the 800s a Brahmin minister replaced the last Turk Shahi king and founded the Hindu Shahi line. Around 870 the Saffarids took Kabul, and the Shahis moved east to the Indus.
